newsitem.title: ZAIRE: New Congo says reactionary forces behind march.
newsitem.headline: New Congo says reactionary forces behind march.

text.p: Laurent Kabila's Democratic Republic of Congo on Saturday blamed reactionary political forces for an anti-Kabila march which was stopped by troops, and said in principle demonstrations were banned.

"In principle demonstrations have not been permitted in all parts of the country that we have liberated in this period of consolidation, but we are very tolerant," information minister Raphael Ghenda told Reuters.
"Today what happened is that reactionary political forces of the former regime manipulated people who claimed to be students."

Troops on Saturday stopped an anti-Kabila march by around one thousand students, a week after the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL) took the capital from soldiers loyal to ousted President Mobutu Sese Seko.
The students were protesting against Kabila's exclusion of popular opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi from his new government and the presence of Rwandan and other African troops among AFDL forces.
Witnesses said about 100 of the students were taken to the Camp Kokolo military barracks near the city centre and were not seen coming out.
"I can assure you that the order had to be maintained and that after some people were removed from the street they were taken straight to their homes," Ghenda said.
Another demonstration by around 150 people in favour of Kabila was allowed to go ahead.
